column1: # Query → the method it should find. Tab-separated: query<TAB>expected<TAB>[provisional]
# DRAFTED BY CLAUDE, NOT YET REVIEWED BY THE OWNER. Every label here is a
# judgement about what a person would mean, and a wrong one makes the eval
# lie in the flattering direction. Veto or amend any line; the harness reads
# this file, so an edit here is the whole change.
# Queries deliberately avoid naming the method, because a query that contains
# the answer only measures string matching. That is what baseline:name is for.
customer owes us money
bills a client has not settled yet
record that a bill was paid
add up what a bill comes to
is this bill past its due date
what a buyer still has to pay
check a password against the stored hash
stop someone signing in
can this user still sign in
full name for showing to a person
validate a bearer token
end a login early
how much space a shape encloses
distance around the outside of a shape
the middle point of a shape
# The tier-separating class. Each of these names something that is in the BODY
# and nowhere in the name, the owner, or the parameters — so the identifier
# tier is structurally unable to answer them and the summary tier should.
# At 21 units the two tiers score the same, which says the corpus is too small
# and too well-named to separate them, not that summaries are worthless. These
# rows are here so that when the corpus grows, the eval can show a difference
# it currently cannot.
retries a few times before giving up
waits longer after each failed attempt
computed once and remembered for later calls
safe to call twice with the same result
hold stock for a customer before checkout
how many units can still be sold
add more units to a shelf
# --- a guard, and the callers that narrate it --------------------------------
# Field-reported (docs/PLAN.md): a question about a check is answered by the
# methods that CALL the guard rather than the one that implements it. Asked in
# keywords here and as a sentence in the natural band, because only one of the
# two phrasings triggers it — which is the finding.
